text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- People's representatives renew pledges of loyalty to Hashemite rule in parliament's response to King Hussein's speech at opening of parliament. Senate Speaker Lawzi says leadership and people are one, Deputies' Speaker Srour says Jordan's unity guarantees stability and progress.

- Crown Prince Hassan, opening conference on Euro-Arab parliamentary dialogue, says only those who believe in peace can be peacemakers. Prince Hassan to leave for Amsterdam today to participate in Middle East conference.
- Prince Hamza bin Hussein has appendix out in London.
- Six-year-old boy killed by poisonous school sandwich in Irbid.
- Prime Minister Kabariti meets Palestinian Authority President Arafat, who stresses importance of King Hussein's efforts to push ahead the Middle East peace process.
- Man accused of poisoning his two children with cyanide says his confessions were made up. Defence lawyers want to test his sanity.
- Cabinet to discuss on Tuesday recommendations of committee charged with implementing King Hussein's amnesty for prisoners.
- Islamist dissident Laith Shubailat says King's pardon was the "height of chivalry".
- Total net profits of 28 service companies on Amman stock Market in first half of 1996 stood at 11 million dinars ($15.5 million), with total revenues at 90 million dinars.
- Kabariti calls for 40 percent increase in budget allocation towards marketing tourism in Jordan in 1997.
- Cabinet approves Finance Minister Awad's budget speech, endorses draft laws on securities and protection for national products.
- Government cuts fodder price by 16 dinars a tonne to reflect world market prices.
